topic_ko: 후광 효과 — 한 가지 좋은 특성이 다른 특성에 대한 판단까지 좌우하므로 실제 특성으로 판단해야 한다

passage: Sometimes one good thing about a person changes how we see everything else about them.
This is known as the halo effect.
If a classmate is great at English, we may assume that he or she is also good at math and science.
We believe this even though we know nothing about the student’s real abilities.
The same thing happens in advertising.
When a famous star promotes a product, people tend to trust the product because they like the star.
In both cases, a first impression shapes our judgment more than the facts do.
So it is wise to judge people and products by their actual qualities.
choices: the importance of learning English well
how celebrities become famous through advertising
ways to make a good first impression on others
why students should study math and science together
how one good quality can affect our overall judgment
theme.explanation_ko: 영어를 잘하는 학생과 연예인 광고의 예를 통해 한 가지 좋은 점이 전체 판단에 영향을 준다는 후광 효과를 설명하므로 ⑤가 주제이다.
theme.distractor_ko: ① 영어 학습은 예시의 소재일 뿐이다. ② 연예인이 유명해지는 과정은 다루지 않는다. ③ 오히려 첫인상보다 사실로 판단하라고 한다. ④ 과목 공부법은 나오지 않는다.

passage: Have you ever thought someone was smart in every subject just because they were good at one?
This is the halo effect at work.
One good quality of a person or product makes us think well of their other qualities too.
For instance, a student who speaks excellent English may seem like a math and science star as well.
Advertising uses this effect when a popular celebrity promotes a product.
Fans often believe the product is excellent simply because they like the celebrity.
Such judgments come from first impressions, not from facts.
We should therefore judge people and products by what they are really like.
choices: 좋은 첫인상을 남기는 것이 성공의 열쇠이다.
유명인이 광고하는 제품은 품질을 믿어도 된다.
한 가지 장점에 휘둘리지 말고 실제 특성으로 판단해야 한다.
영어를 잘하는 학생은 다른 과목도 잘한다.
gist.explanation_ko: 한 가지 좋은 특성 때문에 다른 특성까지 좋게 보는 판단은 첫인상에서 나온 것이므로, 실제 모습으로 판단해야 한다는 ③이 요지이다.
gist.distractor_ko: ① 첫인상을 남기는 법이 아니라 첫인상에 속지 말라는 글이다. ② 연예인 때문에 제품을 믿는 것이 바로 후광 효과이다. ④ 그렇게 ‘보일’ 뿐 실제로는 알 수 없다. ⑤ 광고의 정확성은 다루지 않는다.

passage: Sometimes one good thing about a person changes how we see everything else about them.
This is known as the halo effect.
If a classmate is great at English, we may assume that he or she is also good at math and science.
We believe this even though we know nothing about the student’s real abilities.
The same thing happens in advertising.
When a famous star promotes a product, people tend to trust the product because they like the star.
In both cases, a first impression shapes our judgment more than the facts do.
So it is wise to judge people and products by their actual qualities.
choices: Why English Is the Most Important Subject
One Bright Spot: How the Halo Effect Shapes Our Judgments
Why Famous Stars Sell More Products
Tips for Making a Strong First Impression
The Science of Learning Many Subjects
title.explanation_ko: 한 가지 좋은 점(One Bright Spot)이 판단 전체를 좌우하는 후광 효과를 다루므로 ②가 제목으로 알맞다.
title.distractor_ko: ① 영어가 가장 중요한 과목이라는 내용은 없다(영어는 예시의 소재). ③ 연예인 광고는 예시 중 하나이다. ④ 첫인상을 강하게 남기는 법은 다루지 않는다. ⑤ 여러 과목 학습법은 나오지 않는다.

passage: Imagine meeting a new classmate who speaks English beautifully.
Right away, you may think she is also a top student in math and science.
Yet you have never seen her math test or her science report.
Your opinion grew out of a single strength.
The same thing happens when a famous celebrity promotes a product.
Fans believe the product is excellent simply because they like the star.
In both cases, we are blinded by the light of one bright quality.
To be fair, we should look at actual qualities, not first impressions.
implication.underlined: blinded by the light of one bright quality
choices: unable to see clearly because the room is too bright
confused because the person has no good qualities
impressed by facts that we have carefully checked
jealous of people who are better than us
judging everything by one good point we noticed first
implication.explanation_ko: 영어 실력 하나, 연예인에 대한 호감 하나 때문에 나머지를 확인하지 않고 좋게 판단한다는 뜻이므로 ⑤가 알맞다.
implication.distractor_ko: ① 실제로 눈이 부신 것이 아니다(비유). ② 좋은 특성이 있어서 생기는 일이다. ③ 사실을 확인하지 않았다. ④ 질투는 나오지 않는다.

passage: The halo effect is a psychological phenomenon that affect our judgments.
It happens when one good quality influences how we think about other qualities.
Imagine that you meet a student who is very good at English.
You may think the student is also good at math, even though you do not know the facts.
In advertising, a product promoted by a famous celebrity may seem excellent.
This is simply because people like the celebrity.
So we should try to judge things based on their actual qualities.
grammar.explanation_ko: 주격 관계대명사 that 의 선행사가 단수 명사 a psychological phenomenon 이므로 동사는 affects 가 되어야 한다.
grammar.distractor_ko: ② influences 의 목적어인 간접의문문 「의문사 + 주어 + 동사」. ③ 선행사 a student(사람·단수) + who is. ④ 뒤에 「주어 + 동사」가 오는 양보 접속사 even though. ⑤ 제품이 ‘홍보되는’ 수동 관계이므로 과거분사 promoted.

passage: The halo effect is a common psychological phenomenon.
One good quality of a person can influence how we judge their other qualities.
If a student is good at English, we may assume the student is also good at math.
We think this even though we do not know the student’s actual abilities.
Likewise, people may trust a product because a celebrity they like promotes it.
Such judgments are based on facts rather than first impressions.
Therefore, we should judge people by their real qualities.
vocab.explanation_ko: 실제 능력을 모르면서 판단하고, 연예인이 좋아서 제품을 믿는 것은 사실이 아니라 첫인상에 근거한 판단이므로 ‘first impressions rather than facts’가 되어야 한다.
vocab.distractor_ko: ① 한 가지 특성이 다른 특성의 판단에 ‘영향을 준다’. ② 수학도 잘한다고 ‘가정한다’. ③ ‘실제’ 능력을 모른다. ④ 연예인이 제품을 ‘홍보한다’.

passage: Why do we trust a product just because a famous celebrity promotes it?
The answer lies in the halo effect.
When one good quality stands out, it influences how we see everything else.
A student who is great at English may seem good at math and science too.
A product may seem excellent because we like the person who advertises it.
In other words, our judgments are often shaped by ______________________.
That is why we should try to judge things based on their actual qualities.
choices: the opinions of experts we trust
the prices of the products we buy
blank.explanation_ko: 눈에 띄는 좋은 점 하나 때문에 확인하지 않은 다른 특성까지 좋게 보므로, 판단은 ‘사실보다는 첫인상’에 의해 만들어진다.
blank.distractor_ko: ① 사실에 근거하지 않는다는 것이 핵심이다. ② 전문가 의견, ③ 가격, ⑤ 과거의 실패는 나오지 않는다.

irrelevant.intro: The halo effect happens when one good quality of a person or product influences how we think about their other qualities.
sentences: Learning a second language early can also improve memory skills.
For example, if a student is very good at English, we may think the student is also good at math.
We believe this even though we do not know the student’s actual abilities.
Similarly, when a celebrity we like promotes a product, we may believe the product is excellent.
This shows that our judgments are sometimes influenced by first impressions rather than facts.
irrelevant.explanation_ko: ①은 조기 외국어 학습이 기억력에 주는 효과에 관한 내용으로, 후광 효과를 설명하는 글의 흐름과 무관하다.
irrelevant.distractor_ko: ② 학생 예시, ③ 실제 능력을 모른다는 점, ④ 광고 예시, ⑤ 결론으로 모두 흐름에 맞다.

order.given: The halo effect is an interesting psychological phenomenon. It happens when one good quality influences how we think about other qualities.

blocks.A: The halo effect can also be seen in advertising. When a famous celebrity promotes a product, people may believe the product is excellent just because they like the celebrity.
blocks.B: For example, imagine that you meet a student who is very good at English. You may think the student is also good at math and science without knowing their actual abilities.
blocks.C: These examples show that our judgments are sometimes based on first impressions rather than facts. Therefore, we should judge people and products by their actual qualities.

order.explanation_ko: 후광 효과의 정의(주어진 글) → For example 로 영어 잘하는 학생(B) → can also 로 광고 예시(A) → These examples 로 결론(C) 순이다.
order.distractor_ko: (A)의 also 는 앞에 다른 예가 먼저 나왔음을 뜻하므로 (B) 뒤에 오고, (C)의 These examples 는 두 예시를 모두 받으므로 맨 끝이다.

insert.insert_sentence: People may believe that the product is excellent simply because they like the celebrity.

passage_marked.text: The halo effect happens when one good quality shapes how we see other qualities.
If a student is very good at English, we may think the student is good at math and science too.

insert.explanation_ko: 주어진 문장의 the product 와 the celebrity 는 ④ 앞 문장의 a product 와 a famous celebrity 를 받고, 뒤 문장의 ‘제품에 대한 성급한 결론’이 바로 이 믿음을 가리키므로 ④에 들어간다.
insert.distractor_ko: ①②③ 앞에는 제품과 연예인이 아직 나오지 않았다. ⑤ 마지막 문장이 ‘제품에 대한 결론’을 이미 언급하므로 그 뒤에 오면 순서가 뒤바뀐다.

passage: Have you ever thought someone was smart in every subject just because they were good at one?
This is the halo effect at work.
One good quality of a person or product makes us think well of their other qualities too.
For instance, a student who speaks excellent English may seem like a math and science star as well.
Advertising uses this effect when a popular celebrity promotes a product.
Fans often believe the product is excellent simply because they like the celebrity.
Such judgments come from first impressions, not from facts.

summary.summary_template: Because of the halo effect, one __(A)__ quality can change how we judge other qualities, so we should rely on __(B)__ qualities rather than first impressions.
summary.explanation_ko: 한 가지 좋은(good) 특성이 다른 특성의 판단을 바꾸므로, 첫인상보다 실제(actual) 특성에 근거해야 한다는 요약이다.
summary.distractor_ko: ①⑤ 나쁜 특성이 아니라 좋은 특성이다. ③ 유명한 특성에 의존하라는 내용이 아니다. ④ 숨겨진 특성이 아니라 눈에 띄는 좋은 특성이다.

writing.question: 다음 우리말과 같은 뜻이 되도록 <보기>의 단어를 모두 배열하여 영작하시오.
writing.explanation_ko: 조동사가 있는 수동태 「can + be + 과거분사」(can be seen), 부사 also 는 조동사와 be 사이에 둔다.
writing.answer: The halo effect can also be seen in advertising.
writing.ko_prompt: 후광 효과는 광고에서도 볼 수 있다.

writing.question: 다음 조건에 맞게 우리말을 영작하시오.
conditions: 양보의 접속사 even though 를 사용할 것
be good at 을 사용할 것
writing.explanation_ko: may + 동사원형(may think), 명사절 접속사 that, 양보의 even though + 주어 + 동사를 쓴다.
writing.answer: You may think that the student is also good at math and science, even though you do not know their actual abilities.
writing.ko_prompt: 여러분은 그 학생의 실제 능력을 알지 못하는데도, 그 학생이 수학과 과학도 잘한다고 생각할지도 모른다.

writing.question: 본문의 내용에 맞게 빈칸에 알맞은 한 단어를 쓰시오.
writing.context: The halo effect shows that our judgments are sometimes influenced by first impressions ___________ than facts.

writing.question: 다음 문장을 우리말로 해석하시오.
writing.explanation_ko: when 절의 주어는 one good quality of a person or product(단수 → influences), how we think 는 「의문사 + 주어 + 동사」 간접의문문이다.
writing.en_prompt: It happens when one good quality of a person or product influences how we think about their other qualities.
writing.answer: 그것은 어떤 사람이나 제품의 한 가지 좋은 특성이 그 대상의 다른 특성들에 대해 우리가 생각하는 방식에 영향을 미칠 때 일어난다.

writing.question: 본문을 한 문장으로 요약할 때 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말을 본문에서 찾아 각각 한 단어로 쓰시오.
writing.summary: One good __(A)__ of a person or product can influence how we think about their other qualities, so we should judge them based on their __(B)__ qualities.
writing.explanation_ko: 본문 2번 문장의 one good quality, 8번 문장의 based on their actual qualities 에서 찾는다.

writing.question: 다음 조건에 맞게 이 글의 주제문을 영어로 쓰시오.
writing.ko_prompt: 이 글의 주제를 한 문장으로 쓰시오.
conditions: the halo effect 와 first impressions 를 반드시 포함할 것
writing.answer: The halo effect shows that first impressions, not facts, can influence how we judge people and products.
writing.explanation_ko: 한 가지 좋은 점(첫인상)이 판단을 좌우한다는 내용과 사실이 아니라는 대비를 한 문장에 담는다.
